questions.questionTextEn: Which Indian language, is spoken maximum in the world after Hindi?
questions.questionTextHi: [Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2021] Which Indian language, is spoken maximum in the world after Hindi?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B) Bengali. According to ethnologue 2021, Bengali Indian language is the most spoken language in the world after Hindi among the given options. There are a total of 267.65 million uses of the Bengali language globally. [Jharkhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2021]

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following is the largest linguistic group of India?
questions.questionTextHi: [Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2015] Which one of the following is the largest linguistic group of India?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B) Indo-Aryan. The largest linguistic group of India is Indo-Aryan. This is most important family of Indian languages and comprises of all the principal languages including Hindi, Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Punjabi, Sindhi, Rajasthani, Assamese, Odiya, Kashmiri, Urdu, and Sanskrit. [Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2015]

questions.questionTextHi: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1998] Which one of the following languages belongs to the Austric group?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C) Khasi. The languages of Austric group (Austro-Asiatic) are Khasi, Santhali, Mundari and Bhumij etc. It is language spoken by the Indian tribes. [I.A.S. (Pre) 1998]

questions.questionTextHi: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1997] Consider the map given below : The predominant languages spo ken in the areas marked A, B, C and D are respectively :
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C) Brajbhasha, Awadhi, Bhojpuri and Maithili. In the area marked as ‘A’, Brajbhasha is spoken. In the area marked ‘B’, Awadhi is spoken. questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following was given the classical language status in 2014?
questions.questionTextHi: [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2016] Which of the following was given the classical language status in 2014?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A) Odiya. Odiya became the sixth language of the country to get classical language status on 20 Feb, 2014. Classical language status was given to Tamil in 2004, Sanskrit in 2005, Telugu and Kannada in 2008 and Malayalam in 2013. [Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2016]
